title: Service Level Conditions on the Co-location Allowance at Workplace Cafe Management Program Sites
content:
Where the client holds an office pantry programme standing open and the pantry programme fees invoiced to that client over the twelve months up to the day the invoice is raised reach the pantry co-location threshold, the co-location allowance is the major pantry co-location rate of the escalated fee; where the client holds an office pantry programme standing open and those pantry programme fees fall below that threshold, the co-location allowance is the minor pantry co-location rate of the escalated fee; and where the client holds no office pantry programme standing open, the co-location allowance is the nil co-location rate of the escalated fee.

## Condition

The condition is read off the client's holdings beyond the cafe site. The records consulted are those of the Office Pantry & Beverage Program: whether a programme of that kind held by the same client stands open, and the pantry programme fees invoiced to that client over the twelve months up to the day the invoice is raised, taken from that programme's own charge records.

## Judgement

Two judgements are made, in this order of reading. First, does an office pantry programme held by the client stand open. Second, where one does, do the pantry programme fees invoiced to that client over those 12 months reach the pantry co-location threshold of 45000.00 USD. Fees that exactly equal 45000.00 USD reach the threshold; only fees below 45000.00 USD fall below it.

## Result


| Office pantry programme held by the client | Pantry programme fees invoiced over the 12 months up to the day the invoice is raised | Co-location rate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stands open | Reach 45000.00 USD | The major pantry co-location rate, 6.00 per cent |
| Stands open | Fall below 45000.00 USD | The minor pantry co-location rate, 3.00 per cent |
| None standing open | Not in question | The nil co-location rate, so that no co-location allowance is taken |

## Conditions worked on hypothetical holdings

A client of the Workplace Cafe Management Program is taken, hypothetically, to hold an office pantry programme standing open with pantry programme fees of 51800.00 USD invoiced over those 12 months; those fees reach 45000.00 USD, so the major pantry co-location rate of 6.00 per cent applies, and on a hypothetical escalated fee of 7400.00 USD the co-location allowance is 444.00 USD. Were the pantry programme fees over those 12 months instead 44999.99 USD, they would fall below 45000.00 USD, the minor pantry co-location rate of 3.00 per cent would apply, and the co-location allowance on the same hypothetical escalated fee would be 222.00 USD. Were the client to hold no office pantry programme standing open, the nil co-location rate would apply and no co-location allowance would be taken.
